title: $200 Billion: The Costs of the Iran War
author: Peter Hart
content:
Shortly after the US launched its war on Iran, military officials
[reportedly](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/iran-war-cost-first-week-military-
congress/) told lawmakers that it would cost about $1.5 billion per day. There
were reasons to believe that this was likely an undercount. Those impressions
were bolstered once [reports
surfaced](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/03/18/iran-
cost-budget-pentagon/) that the Pentagon is seeking an additional $200 billion
appropriation from Congress.

Even with a military budget that exceeds $1 trillion, this is a substantial
increase in spending. Since Trump took office, the White House and the
Republican majority in Congress have enacted sharp cuts to social spending and
safety net programs – most prominently as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill
Act (OBBA) – because they thought it necessary to rein in government spending.

On an annual basis, several of the most high profile cuts are estimated to
cost less the Iran war’s $200 billion price tag:

> \+ Medicaid cuts: [$100
> billion](https://www.americanprogress.org/article/1-trillion-in-medicaid-
> cuts-1-trillion-in-tax-giveaways-for-the-richest-1-percent-the-one-big-
> beautiful-bills-budget-math/)
>
> \+ Cuts to the SNAP food assistance program: [$20
> billion](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/08/trumps-spending-bill-cuts-billions-
> in-snap-benefits.html)
>
> \+ Expiration of the enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies: [$30
> billion](https://www.warren.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/icymi-cbo-
> director-confirms-the-cost-of-trumps-war-in-iran-could-cover-health-care-
> for-millions-of-americans)
>
> \+ Recissions package cutting foreign aid and Corporation for Public
> Broadcasting: [$9 billion](https://www.politico.com/news/2025/07/17/senate-
> votes-to-cut-9-billion-from-public-broadcasting-and-foreign-aid-00459199)

The health care cuts are projected to cause millions of people to lose their
coverage. Millions will lose their food assistance, leading to potentially
[tens of thousands](https://www.americanprogress.org/article/snap-cuts-could-
lead-to-70000-avoidable-deaths/) of avoidable deaths.

Trump has [said](https://newrepublic.com/post/208000/donald-trump-iran-war-
cost-food-gas-prices-rise) that the additional war funding is “a small price
to pay to make sure that we stay tippy top.” When it comes to these other
programs, though, evidently the price was too high.

_This first appeared on[CEPR](https://cepr.net/publications/200-billion-the-
costs-of-the-iran-war/)._
